summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, a history of a failed renal transplant, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for recurrent fevers following completion of a prior antibiotic course. Despite extensive workup—including blood and urine cultures, CT, PET scan, echocardiogram, and ultrasound—no definitive source of infection was identified. The fevers persisted at low grade, and the medical team suspected the embolized transplant kidney as a possible source, though biopsy was deemed high-risk due to surgical mesh and bowel proximity. Antibiotics were withheld, and fevers were managed symptomatically. Warfarin was held due to supratherapeutic INR, and clobetasol cream was added for a persistent rash. She was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up and possible biopsy evaluation.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Contact dermatitis and other eczema, unspecified cause
